questions.problem: On a math test, Kevin answered $95%$ of the problems correctly. If he answered $38$ problems correctly, how many problems were on the test?
questions.worked_solution:
We're given a part and a percentage, and we need to find the whole.

In this case, the part is the number of problems answered correctly, which is $38.$ The percentage is $95%,$ and the whole is the total number of problems on the test. 

To solve this question, we can use the following formula:

$$
\text{whole}=\text{part}÷\text{percentage}
$$

Before we can substitute our numbers into the formula, we need to express $95%$ as a fraction:

$$
\frac{95}{100}=\frac{95÷5}{100÷5}=\frac{19}{20}
$$

We can now substitute our numbers into the formula, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{whole} & =38÷95% \\  & =38÷\frac{19}{20} \\  & =38\times \frac{20}{19} \\  & =\frac{38}{19}\times 20 \\  & =2\times 20 \\  & =40\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there were $40$ problems on the test.

questions.problem: A school's softball team lost $18%$ of the games they played last year. If the team lost $9$ games last year, how many games did the team win?
questions.worked_solution:
We need to know the total number of games played to determine the number of games won. 

We're given a part and a percentage, and we need to find the whole.

In this case, the part is the number of games the team lost, which is $9.$ The percentage is $18%,$ and the whole is the total number of games played. 

To find the whole, we can use the following formula:

$$
\text{whole}=\text{part}÷\text{percentage}
$$

Before we can substitute our numbers into the formula, we need to express $18%$ as a fraction:

$$
\frac{18}{100}=\frac{18÷2}{100÷2}=\frac{9}{50}
$$

We can now substitute our numbers into the formula, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{whole} & =9÷18% \\  & =9÷\frac{9}{50} \\  & =9\times \frac{50}{9} \\  & =\frac{9}{9}\times 50 \\  & =50\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the total number of games played by the softball team last year was $50.$ The total number of games won is

$$
50-9=41.
$$

Hence, the softball team won $41$ games last year.

canonical_examples.problem: In the math club, there are $16$ girls and some boys. If the girls represent $40\%$ of the total members of the club, how many members does the math club have?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We're given a part and a percentage, and we need to find the whole.

In this case, the part is the number of girls in the math club, which is $16.$ The percentage is $40\%,$ and the whole is the total number of club members.

To find the whole, we can use the following formula:

$$
\textrm{whole} = \textrm{part} \div \textrm{percentage}
$$

Before we can substitute our numbers into the formula, we need to express $40\%$ as a fraction:

$$
\dfrac{40}{100} = \dfrac{40\div 20}{100\div 20} = \dfrac{2}{5}
$$

We can now substitute our numbers into the formula, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{whole} & =16÷40% \\  & =16÷\frac{2}{5} \\  & =16\times \frac{5}{2} \\  & =\frac{16}{2}\times 5 \\  & =8\times 5 \\  & =40\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the club has $40$ members.

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
To find a part given a percent and whole, we can use the following formula:

$$
\textrm{percent} \times \textrm{whole} = \textrm{part}
$$

However, we sometimes want to find a whole given a part and a percent. To do this, we can use the relationship between multiplication and division to rewrite the above formula as follows:

$$
\textrm{whole} = \textrm{part} \div \textrm{percent}
$$

Let's use this formula to find the missing number in the following statement:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14182311/assets/082c6ac53fa8de85b739dde0611943e92cb09d74d07378d6a33043d4b231e88d.svg)

In this case, the part is $540$, and the percent is $30\%.$ 

We can express $30\%$ as a fraction as follows:

$$
\dfrac{30}{100} = \dfrac{30\div 10}{100\div 10} = \dfrac{3}{10}
$$

Putting these numbers into our formula for the whole, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{whole} & =\text{part}÷\text{percent} \\  & =540÷30% \\  & =540÷\frac{3}{10} \\  & =540\times \frac{10}{3} \\  & =\frac{540}{3}\times 10 \\  & =180\times 10 \\  & =1,800\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing number is $1,800.$
